confirmed_findings.title: Runner cells inherit a 30-minute GPU wait, not the protocol's 7200 s
confirmed_findings.claim: Every one of the 12 training cells and 156 eval cells gates on wait_for_gpu with max_wait = LUCID_GPU_WAIT_SECONDS defaulting to 1800 s; the live queue process (PID 1297554) does not set that variable, so any foreign job holding the GPU below 12000 MiB free for >30 min at a cell boundary raises RuntimeError, kills the runner mid-campaign without a final receipt, and the queue then marks the whole preregistered study failed with no resume path. Project drivers use 7200 s.

confirmed_findings.title: Queue's gpu_idle_gate is one-shot: any GPU occupancy at firing time kills the study permanently

confirmed_findings.title: Known next-episode-credit trap avoided in code but has NO explicit regression test at the capture point
confirmed_findings.claim: Credit correctness rests on one ordering: step_and_observe captures bins = _episode_start_bins(env) (derived from motion_command.motion_start_time_steps, i.e. the episode-start phase of the currently running episode) BEFORE calling observer._original_step. That makes the terminal transition carry the old episode's bin, avoiding the known trap. But no test pins this: the only test that calls _install (test_uninstall_restores_preexisting_instance_attributes_exactly, test_featured_observer.py:410)
